 Live Updates 
 Live updates: Sixers outscored 36-13 in the third quarter 
 Follow along for live updates as the Sixers travel to Indiana to face the Pacers. 
 By Karli Cauley • 
 Published 4 hours ago • 
 Updated 15 minutes ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 Oct 28, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Philadelphia 76ers guard Jaylen Brown (7) dribbles the ball while Indiana Pacers guard Kelly Oubre Jr. (10) defends in the first half at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images
 What to Know
 Tyrese Maxey is averaging 28.8 points per game and earned Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors.
 Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe are off the injury report after missing Sunday’s game.
 The Sixers are averaging 10.5 steals and 11.8 turnovers per game.
 Jabari Walker is out against the Pacers with left knee soreness, marking his second consecutive missed game.
 The Pacers will be without Ivica Zubac, former Sixer T.J. McConnell and Tyrese Haliburton (left hamstring tightness), while Andrew Nembhard (neck soreness) is questionable.
 Tip off begins at 7:00 p.m. ET on NBC Sports Philadelphia. 
 FROM THE LOGO 🗣️
 View this post on Instagram 
 Up 🔟
 Anfernee Simons breaks through after three-game shooting skid
 Oct 24, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers guard Anfernee Simons (5) controls the ball against the Milwaukee Bucks during the second quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images 
 Anfernee Simons entered Wednesday night needing to see a few shots fall.
 He saw four of them drop before halftime.
 Simons scored 12 points on four three-pointers, helping the Sixers take a 62-52 lead over the Pacers into the break. He finished the half 4 for 7 from beyond the arc, landing one point shy of his season high before the third quarter began.
 It was also one more point than he had scored over his previous three games combined.
 After making 5 of 10 shots and scoring 13 points in the season opener against the Knicks, Simons went 3 for 21 from the field and 2 for 13 from three over the next three games. He scored two points against Cleveland, four against Milwaukee and five against Detroit.
 The slow start came after a hamstring injury kept Simons out for much of training camp and the entire preseason. He has been learning where his shots will come from while attempting to regain his rhythm during regular-season games.
 That rhythm arrived quickly in the second quarter Wednesday.
 Simons made his first three off a LeBron James assist with 9:50 remaining, giving the Sixers a 34-30 lead. James found him again on Philadelphia’s next possession, and Simons knocked down another from long range just 22 seconds later.
 Two more followed before halftime. His fourth three accounted for Philadelphia’s fifth make from beyond the arc as a team.
 The sequence offered a look at how Simons can fit alongside the Sixers’ stars. He did not need to dominate the ball or manufacture difficult shots. James drew the defense, delivered the pass and allowed Simons to fire before Indiana could recover.
 Simons has averaged more than 17 points in five different NBA seasons. The question was never whether he could make shots. It was how quickly he could find a steady role after missing the preseason and joining a lineup filled with players accustomed to controlling the ball.
 Four first-half threes do not settle that question, but they represented his most productive stretch since joining the Sixers—and helped create their 10-point halftime advantage.
